market_holds: Spot $1.755 at the 2026-11-13 seal, which is 0.9% above the 52-week low and 58% below the high. The stock is -8.1% over 20 days and -29% since the 2026-08-07 close of $2.46, the last close before the Q2 print. There is no usable option chain (empty front expiry), so no implied move. The baseline history mixes volume updates with earnings. The four true earnings days were about -6.9% (2025-11-17, read as bmo), -1.0% (2026-03-16/18), -14.8% (2026-05-18) and -17.1% (2026-08-10), so all four were negative and the median absolute is about 11%. Q3 volume came out 2026-10-05: 537,457 units, +15.4%; China +8.6%, international +226%. The stock rose about 3% that day and has drifted down since. The only guide is Q3 revenue of RMB 1,863-2,033m (+10-20% y/y), given 2026-08-10. There is no margin guide. The March FY2026 volume target was 1.67-1.91m units, and I found nothing saying whether it was kept in August. Coverage is very thin: 3 analysts in March, and the revenue consensus came from one of them. I could find no current Q3 consensus. Short interest is 0.5% of shares (FINRA 2026-10-30, per the sweep row). Market cap is about $140m against RMB 1,476m (about $207m) of cash and investments at 2026-06-30, so the stock trades below gross cash.
view: Two things will decide this print: whether Q3 revenue reaches the low end of the August guide, and gross margin in the peak quarter. Q4's guide comes third. The volume is already public, so the revenue can be rebuilt. I took China at 490,406 units and international at 47,051 units at about RMB 3,270, the Q2 blended international price, which gives about RMB 150m; accessories I put at RMB 150-185m. On those inputs, the low end of RMB 1,863m needs China revenue per scooter of about RMB 3,190, which is -3% y/y. In Q2 China revenue per scooter was RMB 3,010, -9.2% y/y, because e-motorcycles reached about 60% of China volume and sell at lower prices and margins. At Q2's price level Q3 revenue comes out around RMB 1,800m, about 3% below the low end. That would be the second straight quarter below the company's own floor; Q2's RMB 1,440m was 8% under. Margins: China peers say input costs rose in Q3. Aima's Q3 gross margin was 16.8%, down 1.9pp on the quarter, and Segway-Ninebot also cites higher raw-material costs. So NIU's gross margin is likely about 15-17% against 21.8% a year ago. With operating expenses running near RMB 340m+ a quarter, that points to a net loss in what is seasonally the strongest quarter, against RMB 81.7m of profit in Q3 2025. Year to date volume is 1.23m units, so even the low end of the March FY target needs about 436k units in Q4, against 173k in Q4 2025. Any Q4 guide will in effect show that target being missed. On the other side, Q4 2025 was depressed by the end of old-standard sales (revenue RMB 676m, -17%), so the Q4 guide will probably print a large y/y growth figure. The stock also sits at its low, below gross cash, with almost no short interest. History cuts against that rescue. This name has sold off on every earnings day for a year, including after good headlines: +65% revenue in Q3 2025 still closed about -7%, and a strong Q2 guide in May came with -14.8%. In Q2 the market did not do the volume-to-revenue arithmetic before the print and fell 17% on the day. My view is that the print is more likely to disappoint than not, but the price has already fallen about 29% since the last print. That makes the size of the gap uncertain, though not its sign. Direction leans down, short of a recommendation.
unpriced: Possibly the volume-implied revenue shortfall and the Q3 swing to a loss. Coverage is three analysts with one revenue estimate, nothing current for Q3 is visible, and in Q2 the same arithmetic was not priced before the print. I cannot show what the price holds, though: the 29% fall since August and the 10% drift since the volume release may already contain it.

recommendation.reason: Rebuilding revenue from the disclosed Q3 volume and Q2 prices puts it near RMB 1,800m, under the RMB 1,863m low end of the guide. China peers show margin pressure in Q3, and the stock has fallen on all four of its last earnings days. The stock has already fallen about 29% since the last print and trades below gross cash, and a strong-looking Q4 y/y guide on an easy base could rescue the morning. So the downside lean does not reach 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 revenue at or above RMB 1,863m with gross margin at or above 18%, plus a Q4 guide implying 50%+ y/y growth. That would mean China prices held near last year's despite the e-motorcycle mix, and the miss-every-quarter story would break.

self_critique: The stock has already fallen 29% since the Q2 print, sits at its 52-week low and below gross cash, and has almost no short interest. Anyone who can do the volume arithmetic has had six weeks to sell. International units tripled and could carry a higher price than I assumed, accessories could grow faster, and the Q4 guide will show large y/y growth on a depressed base. A merely in-line print could bounce a stock this washed out by the 13:00 window.
approach_notes: The 'freshest data first' rule and own-arithmetic (rebuilding revenue from the disclosed volume) helped most, and so did the peer read-through for margins. The baseline's reaction history mixed volume updates with earnings and had to be re-read by hand. Thin coverage made 'priced in is a claim to prove' unanswerable either way.
